welcome.text: sonde runs a program, signs its requests with your endpoint's credentials and reads them as operations — multipart uploads, retries, SlateDB, Iceberg, Delta and Lance steps. A run can then be tried under faults: the same command with the store slowing down, failing or losing an answer.

why.obs.unfinished: An upload that is started and never completed or aborted keeps its parts. They are billed as storage, invisible to listings, until an abort or a lifecycle rule (AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload) removes them.
why.obs.orphans: Data files written with no commit after them belong to no version of the table. A failed or abandoned write leaves them; only a cleanup (vacuum, orphan-file removal) deletes them.
why.obs.small: A multipart upload takes at least three requests (create, part, complete). Under the part size threshold a single PUT does the same in one, faster and cheaper.
why.obs.hot: One key read again and again. Each read is a request and a round trip; a cache in front of it would remove most of them.
why.obs.listed: Listing the same prefix again and again is slow (a page per 1000 keys) and billed per request; a manifest, or a listing kept between calls, avoids it.

why.obs.headget: Each HEAD is a request and a round trip before the read. A GET returns the same headers with the body; a missing object answers 404 to either.
why.obs.throttled: The store refused requests to protect itself; each one was retried or failed. Capping requests in flight, or spreading keys over more prefixes, keeps under its limit.
why.obs.throttled.rate: The store refused requests to protect itself, even with few in flight: the rate per prefix is the limit. Back off with jitter, or spread keys over more prefixes.

phrase.trial.advice.retry: send a failed request again: a 500, 502, 503, 504, 408 or 429 is owed a retry, and so is S3's SlowDown, RequestTimeout or RequestTimeTooSkewed
phrase.trial.advice.skew: a 403 RequestTimeTooSkewed is owed a retry signed again by the clock the answer's Date gives (the AWS SDKs for Java and JavaScript do this; boto3 does not); and keep the machine's clock in time
phrase.trial.advice.timeout: give each attempt a timeout well under a stall (a first byte comes in well under a second), so that a stalled request is sent again
phrase.trial.advice.list: a listing just after a write may not show it yet: keep the keys the program wrote, or list again before going on without one
phrase.trial.advice.cut: check the bytes read against Content-Length, and read the rest (Range) or the whole again
phrase.trial.advice.race: on a 412, read the log again and write the next commit with its condition; never write the key without one

core.probe.cond.put-if-none-match.title: PUT If-None-Match: *
core.probe.cond.put-if-none-match.descri: Create-only writes: a PUT with If-None-Match: * succeeds on a new key and is refused when the key exists.
core.probe.cond.put-if-none-match.aws: First PUT 200; second PUT 412 PreconditionFailed (409 ConditionalRequestConflict while a concurrent write is in flight). The object keeps its first body.
core.probe.cond.put-if-match.title: PUT If-Match
core.probe.cond.put-if-match.description: Compare-and-swap writes: a PUT with If-Match succeeds only while the object still has that ETag.
core.probe.cond.put-if-match.aws: PUT with a stale ETag: 412 PreconditionFailed; with the current ETag: 200. A missing key with If-Match: 404 NoSuchKey.
core.probe.cond.copy-if-match.title: Conditional CopyObject
core.probe.cond.copy-if-match.descriptio: CopyObject with x-amz-copy-source-if-match (on the source) and If-None-Match: * (on the destination).
core.probe.cond.copy-if-match.aws: Wrong source ETag: 412; destination exists with If-None-Match: *: 412; otherwise 200.
core.probe.cond.complete-if-none-match.d: CompleteMultipartUpload with If-None-Match: * when the key was created in the meantime.
core.probe.cond.complete-if-none-match.a: 412 PreconditionFailed; the existing object is kept. The upload can still be aborted.

core.probe.checksum.trailing.title: Trailing checksum (aws-chunked)
core.probe.checksum.trailing.description: PUT with Content-Encoding: aws-chunked, STREAMING-UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD-TRAILER and an x-amz-checksum-crc32 trailer: what current AWS SDKs send by default.
core.probe.checksum.trailing.aws: 200; the trailer's CRC32 is verified, stored and returned by HEAD; the stored body is the decoded payload (no chunk framing).
core.probe.mpu.min-part-size.title: Minimum part size
core.probe.mpu.min-part-size.description: Completes an upload whose first part is 1 MiB (every part but the last must be at least 5 MiB).
core.probe.mpu.min-part-size.aws: 400 EntityTooSmall at CompleteMultipartUpload; a 5 MiB first part completes.
core.probe.mpu.out-of-order.title: Parts out of order
core.probe.mpu.out-of-order.description: Uploads part 2 before part 1, completes with the parts listed in descending order, then in ascending order.
core.probe.mpu.out-of-order.aws: Parts may be uploaded in any order. A Complete listing parts out of ascending order: 400 InvalidPartOrder. Ascending: 200, the body in part-number order.
core.probe.mpu.duplicate-complete.title: Complete twice
core.probe.mpu.duplicate-complete.descri: Sends the same CompleteMultipartUpload twice, as a client retrying after a lost response would.
core.probe.mpu.duplicate-complete.aws: The retry answers 200 with the same ETag (S3 treats a repeated Complete of a just-completed upload as success); afterwards the upload id is gone (NoSuchUpload).
core.probe.mpu.concurrent-same-key.title: Concurrent uploads of one key
core.probe.mpu.concurrent-same-key.descr: Starts two uploads of the same key, completes A, then B.
core.probe.mpu.concurrent-same-key.aws: Two distinct upload ids; both complete; the last Complete wins (the key holds B's body).
core.probe.mpu.upload-part-copy.title: UploadPartCopy
core.probe.mpu.upload-part-copy.descript: Builds an object from a byte range of another with UploadPartCopy, plus an uploaded part.
core.probe.mpu.upload-part-copy.aws: 200 with <CopyPartResult>; the completed object holds the copied range followed by the uploaded part.
core.probe.range.bounds.title: Range boundaries
core.probe.range.bounds.description: GETs bytes=0-0, bytes=9-9, bytes=-3 (suffix), bytes=7- (open) and bytes=5-100 (past the end) of a 10-byte object.
core.probe.range.bounds.aws: 206 Partial Content for each, with Content-Range bytes a-b/10; a range past the end is cut to the object (bytes 5-9/10).
core.probe.range.multi.title: Multiple ranges
core.probe.range.multi.aws: S3 does not serve multiple ranges: it ignores such a header and answers 200 with the whole object.
core.probe.range.unsatisfiable.title: Range past the end
core.probe.range.unsatisfiable.descripti: GET bytes=100-200 of a 10-byte object, and bytes=0- of an empty object.
core.probe.range.unsatisfiable.aws: 416 InvalidRange with Content-Range: bytes */10; on an empty object 416 as well.
core.probe.keys.special.title: Special characters and Unicode in keys
core.probe.keys.special.description: PUTs, GETs and lists 14 keys with spaces, +, %, reserved characters, dot segments, // and non-ASCII; the verdict is of the keys sent (sonde cannot send the two with a dot segment).
core.probe.keys.special.aws: Keys are opaque UTF-8: every key round-trips through PUT, GET and ListObjectsV2 (with encoding-type=url) exactly.
core.probe.list.token-stability.title: Continuation token stability
core.probe.list.token-stability.descript: Lists 30 keys 10 at a time; between pages, adds keys before and after the position, then reuses the first token.
core.probe.list.token-stability.aws: A continuation token is a position: later pages continue after the last key returned, include keys written after it, never repeat keys, and the same token can be used again.
core.probe.list.start-after.title: ListObjectsV2 StartAfter
core.probe.list.start-after.description: Lists with StartAfter set to an existing key, to a key between two keys, and to a key outside the prefix.
core.probe.list.start-after.aws: Keys strictly after StartAfter, in UTF-8 binary order; StartAfter is echoed in the response.
core.probe.delete.batch-limit.title: DeleteObjects batch limit
core.probe.delete.batch-limit.descriptio: DeleteObjects with 1000 keys, then with 1001 (keys that do not exist: nothing is deleted for real).
core.probe.delete.batch-limit.aws: 1000 keys: 200, each key reported deleted (deleting a missing key succeeds). 1001 keys: 400 MalformedXML.
core.probe.presign.expiry.title: Presigned URL expiry
core.probe.presign.expiry.description: Presigns a GET valid for a few seconds (allowing for the difference between this clock and the store's), uses it at once and again once it has expired; presigns with X-Amz-Expires over 7 days.
core.probe.presign.expiry.aws: Fresh URL: 200. Expired: 403 AccessDenied ("Request has expired"). X-Amz-Expires above 604800: 400 AuthorizationQueryParametersError.
core.probe.presign.clock-skew.title: Clock skew tolerance
core.probe.presign.clock-skew.descriptio: Signs requests with the clock 5 minutes ahead, then 20 minutes ahead.
core.probe.presign.clock-skew.aws: 5 minutes: accepted. Beyond 15 minutes: 403 RequestTimeTooSkewed, whose body gives the server's time.
core.probe.meta.size-limit.title: User metadata size limit
core.probe.meta.size-limit.description: PUTs with 1.9 KiB and 2.1 KiB of x-amz-meta-* (names and values).
core.probe.meta.size-limit.aws: Up to 2 KiB of user metadata: 200, returned verbatim by HEAD. Over 2 KiB: 400 MetadataTooLarge.
core.probe.version.id-format.title: Version ID format
core.probe.version.id-format.description: Enables versioning on a temporary bucket, writes a key twice and inspects the version ids.
core.probe.version.id-format.aws: Opaque, unique, URL-safe ids (32 characters today); `null` only for writes made while versioning was off or suspended.
core.probe.lock.retention.title: Object Lock retention
core.probe.lock.retention.description: Creates a bucket with Object Lock, writes an object in GOVERNANCE mode for one day, then tries to delete that version.
core.probe.lock.retention.aws: Deleting a locked version: 403 AccessDenied; GetObjectRetention returns the mode and date; a plain DELETE adds a delete marker.
core.probe.sse-c.title: SSE-C
core.probe.sse-c.description: Writes an object with a customer key, reads it without the key, with a wrong key and with the right key.
core.probe.sse-c.aws: PUT with the key: 200. GET without it: 400 InvalidRequest; with a wrong key: 403 AccessDenied; with the right key: 200. Over plain HTTP S3 refuses SSE-C altogether (400).
core.probe.express.append.title: S3 Express append (x-amz-write-offset-bytes)
core.probe.express.append.description: Appends to an object with PUT x-amz-write-offset-bytes at its size, then at a wrong offset.
core.probe.express.append.aws: Directory buckets (S3 Express One Zone): the append succeeds and a wrong offset gives 400 InvalidWriteOffset. General purpose buckets: 501 NotImplemented.
